sol.note: Read `1/3` in the day-of-week field as Monday and Thursday. The spec says `N/S` runs up to the field's maximum, and day of week goes up to 7, so Sunday counts too.

fable.note: Turned 7 into 0 before expanding ranges, so `0-7/2` meant only Sunday instead of Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. That day's spec treats 7 as 0 only in a range that wraps, and `0-7` doesn't.

luna.note: The same `0-7/2` mistake as Fable, `1/3` stopping at Saturday like Sol on Oct 27, and it rejected `"  @hourly "` even though the spec says leading and trailing whitespace is ignored.

sonnet.note: Never added the duplicate key check that the `parse_fields` docstring asks for, and accepted `L/2` in the day-of-month field, where the spec allows `L` only on its own.

luna.note: Rejected every stepped range such as `11-22/5` as "names are not allowed with steps", which caused 23 of its 25 misses. Its day names were also off by one, so `MON` meant Sunday.

astra.note: Read `1/3` in the day-of-week field as Monday and Thursday. The spec says `N/S` runs up to the field's maximum, and day of week goes up to 7, so Sunday counts too. The same mistake Sol made on Oct 27.

luna.note: Took `L` only when it was the whole day-of-month field, so `5-19,L` raised `ValueError`. The spec lists `L` as an item, which can sit in a comma-separated list like any other.

sonnet.note: Accepted `L/2` in the day-of-month field. The spec allows a step only on `*`, a number or a range, so `L` has to stand on its own.

astra.note: Read `1/3` in the day-of-week field as Monday and Thursday. The spec says `N/S` runs up to the field's maximum, and day of week goes up to 7, so Sunday counts too.

luna.note: Rejected `?` in the day-of-week field, so `0 7 ? * ?` raised `ValueError`. The spec allows `?` as a whole day-of-month or day-of-week field.

sonnet.note: Accepted `L/2` in the day-of-month field. The spec allows a step only on `*`, a number or a range, so `L` has to stand on its own. The same miss as the day before.

luna.note: Day names were off by one, so `MON` meant Sunday and `FRI-MON` started on Thursday. A day-of-week field of `?` also matched no day at all, when it should mean the same as `*`.

haiku.note: Two separate mistakes: it accepted `L/2` in the day-of-month field, where `L` has to stand on its own, and it read `1/3` in the day-of-week field as Monday and Thursday, leaving out Sunday (7).

luna.note: Day names were off by one again, so `MON` meant Sunday and `Tue` meant Monday. All four misses use a day name; the same schedules written with numbers work.

fable.note: Rejected any item with an `L` in it outside the day fields, to catch a misplaced `L` or `5L`. That also threw out the month name `JUL`, so `1,JUL` raised `ValueError`.

luna.note: Day names were off by one for the third day running, so `MON` meant Sunday. All three misses use a day name.
